label: NO2
definition: How much nitrogen dioxide, a gas released mainly by burning fuel, sits in the air column above the area, measured by the Aura satellite.
reading_hint: Higher usually means more combustion (traffic, power, industry, fires), but weather also moves it.

label: Wind speed
definition: How fast the wind blows 10 metres above the ground.
reading_hint: Stronger wind spreads pollution out; calm air lets it build up.

label: Cloud amount
definition: The share of the sky covered by cloud.
reading_hint: Clouds also block the satellite's view, so this helps judge how much to trust NO₂ months.

label: Pressure
definition: The air pressure at the ground.
reading_hint: High pressure usually means calm, clear weather; low pressure means storms and cloud.

label: Clear-sky sunlight
definition: The sunlight that would reach the ground if the sky were cloud-free.
reading_hint: Set by the season and latitude; it is the sunny-day ceiling.

label: Cloud sunlight reduction
definition: How much sunlight the clouds blocked: clear-sky sunlight minus actual sunlight.
reading_hint: Larger means cloudier skies took away more sun.

label: Vegetation fire density
definition: How many satellite-detected heat spots from presumed vegetation fires appear per 1,000 km² each day.
reading_hint: Higher means more burning detected, from wildfires, farm burning or war-related fires; the satellite cannot say which.

label: Static heat sources
definition: Heat spots on land that are not vegetation fires, such as gas flares and industrial sites.
reading_hint: A steady background reading; changes can mean industry started, stopped or was damaged.

label: Air temperature
definition: The average air temperature 2 metres above the ground.
reading_hint: The basic measure of warm or cold.

label: Peak temperature
definition: The hottest air temperature reached each day, averaged over the month.
reading_hint: Shows daytime heat, which drives drought and wildfire risk.

label: Temperature range
definition: The gap between the hottest and coldest air temperature of the day.
reading_hint: A big gap means clear, dry days and cold nights; a small gap means cloudy or humid weather.

label: All-sky sunlight
definition: The sunlight actually reaching the ground, with clouds included.
reading_hint: Less than clear-sky sunlight whenever it is cloudy.

label: Evaporation demand (PET)
definition: How much water the air and sun could pull from a well-watered field in a day (the FAO-56 standard estimate).
reading_hint: Higher means thirstier air and faster drying of soil and crops.

label: Rainfall
definition: The rain and snow that fell, as millimetres of water per day.
reading_hint: The main supply of water to land.

label: VPD (drying demand)
definition: How dry the air is, measured as how much more moisture it could still hold.
reading_hint: Higher means the air pulls water from plants and soil harder.

label: Specific humidity
definition: The weight of water vapour in the air, in grams per kilogram of air.
reading_hint: Higher means the air holds more moisture.

label: Relative humidity
definition: How full of water vapour the air is, as a percentage of the most it could hold at that temperature.
reading_hint: Low values mean dry air.

label: Transpiration
definition: The water that plants release into the air through their leaves, per day.
reading_hint: Higher means growing vegetation is active and using water.

label: Water balance (P - PET)
definition: Rainfall minus the water the air could evaporate: the surplus or deficit of water.
reading_hint: Below zero means more water is being demanded than rain supplies.

label: Surface soil wetness
definition: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is, from 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated).
reading_hint: Reacts quickly to rain and dry spells.

label: Root-zone wetness
definition: How wet the soil is down to 1 metre, where most roots grow, from 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated).
reading_hint: Shows whether crops and plants have water in reserve.

label: Full-profile wetness
definition: How wet the whole soil column is, from 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated).
reading_hint: Changes slowly; shows long dry or wet periods.

label: Surface temperature
definition: The temperature of the ground surface itself, not the air above it.
reading_hint: Rises with sun and dry ground.

label: Surface-air diff
definition: How much hotter or cooler the ground surface is than the air just above it.
reading_hint: A large positive gap points to hot, dry, bare ground.

label: Albedo
definition: The share of incoming sunlight the ground reflects, from 0 (none) to 1 (all).
reading_hint: Snow and bright soil reflect more; dark forest and wet fields reflect less.
